name: THS4551IRGTR
title: Low-noise, precision, 150-MHz fully differential amplifier
summary: The THS4551 is a fully differential amplifier for driving differential-input ADCs from single-ended or differential sources: 150 MHz bandwidth at a gain of 1, 135 MHz gain-bandwidth, 3.3 nV/√Hz input noise and a trimmed offset of ±175 µV maximum at 25 °C. Its input range reaches the negative rail and its output swings to within about 0.2 V of either rail, with the output common mode set by the VOCM pin or left at midsupply. It runs from a single 2.7-V to 5.4-V supply on 1.37 mA, has a power-down pin, and comes in 8-pin VSSOP, 10-pin WQFN and 16-pin VQFN packages rated –40 °C to +125 °C.

(4) VOCM control figures run from the VOCM input pin to the average of the two output voltages.

circuits.title: Gain-of-1 characterization circuit, single-ended 50-Ω source to differential output
circuits.description: The bench circuit behind most of the typical curves. A 50-Ω network-analyser source drives RG1 with RT1 making the input look like 50 Ω; the unused input side copies the same impedances with RS1, RT2 and RG2. RF1 and RF2 set a gain of 1 V/V. Two 487-Ω resistors and the 52.3-Ω RM load the outputs with 1 kΩ differential and feed an ADTL1-4-75+ balun into the analyser's 50-Ω input, with 31.8 dB insertion loss from the output pins to the 50-Ω load. PD is tied to VS+ and VOCM is left open.
notes: T1 pins: N1A and N1B are the ends of winding N1, N2A and N2B of winding N2.

circuits.title: Output interface for dc-coupled differential step tests
circuits.description: Each amplifier output drives a 475-Ω resistor into a 50-Ω scope input, with a 56.2-Ω resistor from that node to ground. Each side loads its output with 500 Ω to ground, 1 kΩ differential, and shows the scope a 50-Ω source; the two traces are subtracted to give the differential step response.

circuits.title: Output common-mode test circuit
circuits.description: The VOCM pin is driven from a matched 50-Ω source (RS, RT). Both gain resistors return to ground, so there is no differential input. Two 100-Ω resistors average the outputs into a 50-Ω source for the measuring instrument.

circuits.title: Single-ended to differential, gain of 1 V/V, 50-Ω input match with standard values
circuits.description: A 50-Ω source drives RG1 through its own 50 Ω; RT (52.3 Ω) to ground brings the input impedance to about 50 Ω. On the other input one 1.02-kΩ resistor to ground stands in for the source, RT and RG1 combined. RF1 = RF2 = 1 kΩ gives 1 V/V from the RT node to the differential output across the 1-kΩ load. VOCM is open, so the output sits at midsupply.

circuits.title: AC-coupled single-ended to differential, gain of 2, single 3.3-V supply
circuits.description: A gain-of-2 matched design reduced to its Thevenin source (25.6 Ω, ±1.022 V) and ac-coupled through 1-µF capacitors on both inputs. With VOCM open (1 µF to ground) the outputs and inputs sit at 1.65 V; a 4-VPP differential output swings each output from 0.65 V to 2.65 V, and the input pins move ±0.34 V around 1.65 V.

circuits.title: DC-coupled single-ended to differential attenuator, gain of 0.2 V/V
circuits.description: A ±18-V ground-referenced source is attenuated by 4.99-kΩ / 1-kΩ resistors to a 7.2-VPP differential output for a SAR ADC on a single 5-V supply. VOCM is half of a 4.096-V reference (two 10-kΩ resistors, 1 µF), 2.048 V. The 3.1-pF feedback capacitors and the 2.6-pF capacitor across the inputs shape the noise gain from 1.2 to 3 at high frequency, giving a flat response of about 45 MHz. The input pins sit at 1.71 V and swing ±1.5 V; the source sinks 0.34 mA of common-mode current and sees about 5.44 kΩ.

parts.note: keep the 1-kΩ load: without it the stage can oscillate

notes: Design figures: NG1 = 1.2, NG2 = 3, GBP = 135 MHz, ZO = 14.3 MHz.

circuits.title: DC-coupled gain of 1 with RF = 1 kΩ and a matched 50-Ω single-ended input
circuits.description: The gain-of-1 matched design on a single 5-V supply with VOCM driven to 2.5 V. It is the circuit worked through for the output dc error and drift budget: with standard values G1 = 1000 / 1025.6 and G2 = 1000 / 1020 differ before any resistor tolerance.

circuits.title: AC-coupled differential input to differential output
circuits.description: A differential source is coupled through 10-nF capacitors into 499-Ω gain resistors, with a 1.02-kΩ resistor across the two coupled nodes as the input termination. RF = 1.02 kΩ. With no dc path for the common mode, the input pins sit at the VOCM voltage (open, 1 µF to ground, midsupply of 3.3 V) and do not move with the signal.

circuits.title: DC-coupled differential I/O from a precision dual op amp to an 18-bit SAR ADC
circuits.description: An OPA2192 pair on ±15 V forms a differential gain stage (2 kΩ, 2 kΩ, 200 Ω: 21 V/V differential, 1 V/V common mode). The THS4551 on 5 V attenuates by 0.2 V/V (4.99 kΩ in, 1 kΩ feedback) and resets the common mode to the 2.048 V VOCM taken from a 4.096-V reference, for an ADS9110. 22-pF feedback capacitors and 49 pF across the inputs shape the noise gain; 10 Ω and 12 nF filter into the ADC inputs.

circuits.title: 500-kHz multiple-feedback low-pass filter driving the ADS127L01
circuits.description: A gain-of-1, single-ended to differential, second-order MFB filter (F0 = 500 kHz, Q = 0.63, –3 dB at 443 kHz) on a 3-V supply, driving a 24-bit delta-sigma ADC. 1.2-kΩ input and feedback resistors, 470 pF across the first nodes, 330 Ω into the summing nodes and 270 pF from each output pin back to its input form the filter. The 5-Ω resistors inside the loop and the 1 nF across the inputs only add phase margin. 10 Ω and 22 nF filter into AINN and AINP. Measured with the ADS127L01 at 4 kHz: THD –114 dBc, SNR 106 dB.

circuits.title: Divide-by-10 attenuator, gain of 0.1 V/V
circuits.description: 10-kΩ input and 1-kΩ feedback resistors on ±2.5-V supplies with VOCM grounded. The low noise gain (NG1 = 1.1) leaves about 32° of phase margin and a response peaked by about 5 dB near the top of the band.

circuits.title: Divide-by-10 attenuator with noise-gain compensation capacitors
circuits.description: The 0.1-V/V attenuator with 8.4 pF across each feedback resistor and 16.8 pF across the inputs. Solving for GBP = 135 MHz, NG1 = 1.1, NG2 = 5 and RF = 1 kΩ gives ZO = 3.5 MHz, CF = 9 pF (8.4 pF after the internal 0.6 pF) and CS = 36 pF single-ended, halved to 18 pF across the inputs and less the internal 1.2 pF. The response flattens to about 24 MHz; output noise rises above 3.5 MHz.

circuits.title: Single-ended to differential gain of 10 with a feedback pole
circuits.description: Gain of 10 V/V (200 Ω in, 2 kΩ feedback) band-limited at 320 kHz by 250 pF across each feedback resistor, on a single 5-V supply with only a 10-nF noise capacitor on VOCM. 10 Ω and 10 nF filter into the SAR ADC. At high frequency the feedback capacitors bring noise gain down to 1 V/V and the response measured at the output pins resonates near 50 MHz.

circuits.title: Gain of 10 with a feedback pole and a differential input capacitor
circuits.description: The feedback-pole stage with a 250-pF capacitor across the inputs, equal to the feedback capacitors. The high-frequency noise gain rises from 1 V/V to 3 V/V, the loop crosses over lower with more phase margin, and the 50-MHz resonance is much reduced.

circuits.title: 100-kHz Butterworth MFB filter, gain of 0.2 V/V, into a SAR ADC
circuits.description: Takes a 40-VPP single-ended swing (from an OPA192) to an 8-VPP differential SAR input: gain 0.2 V/V, second-order 100-kHz Butterworth, VOCM = 2.048 V (half a 4.096-V reference), 5-V supply. 2.96 kΩ and 1.5 nF form the first section; 1.57 kΩ into the summing nodes, 592 Ω feedback and 910 pF from each output pin back to its input complete it. 20 Ω inside the loop isolates the load; 10 Ω into 2.2 nF differential with 100 pF to ground on each side filters into the ADC. 100 fF across the inputs marks a place for a differential input capacitor. SNR to the ADC pins is 113 dB for 8 VPP full scale.

circuits.title: Differential transimpedance stage for the PCM1792A current-output audio DAC
circuits.description: The DAC's complementary current outputs feed the two summing nodes directly. Each DAC output also carries a fixed 6.2-mA center current, sunk by a 402-Ω resistor to the –2.5-V rail so the DAC outputs and amplifier inputs stay at ground. ±2.5 V comes from an LM27762; VOCM is grounded. 750-Ω feedback gives 1.5 kΩ differential transimpedance (63.5 dBΩ): 7.8 mAPP full scale becomes ±1.46 V on each output, 5.85 VPP differential. 2.4 nF with 4.4 Ω in series across each feedback resistor sets 88 kHz; 20 nF across the inputs lifts noise gain at high frequency to 17.7 V/V.
notes: I1 and I2 stand for the dc part of the DAC's output current, pin 1 at ground and pin 2 at the summing node.

circuits.title: ADC3241 driver with a second-order RLC interstage filter
circuits.description: A ground-centered 50-Ω source is matched with RT1 = 59 Ω and amplified by 5 V/V (187 Ω and 215 Ω in, 1 kΩ feedback) on a single 3.3-V supply. The ADC's 0.95-V common-mode output drives VOCM. A 10-MHz second-order Bessel filter (40.2 Ω, 390 nH, 360 pF and 732 Ω, all differential) adds –1 dB and passes the common mode unshifted; 5.6 Ω at each ADC input spreads the sampling glitch. Full scale is ±0.2 V at the RT node, 1.8 VPP (–1 dBFS) at the ADC. The input pins swing from 79 mV to 0.256 V. At 25 MSPS the ADC draws 37.5 µA common-mode current, shifting its input common mode by 1.7 mV.

operation.text: A high-gain differential voltage-feedback core drives the two outputs. Two 5.2-kΩ resistors across the outputs sense their average, and a VCM error amplifier compares that with the VOCM pin, or with a 300-kΩ / 300-kΩ divider across the supplies when the pin is open; at dc the sensing resistors set a 10.5-kΩ open-loop output impedance. The large input transistors give 1.2 pF across the inputs, offset by 0.6-pF capacitors inside from each output to its input; count these 0.6 pF when choosing an external feedback capacitor. Disabling the part also turns off the midsupply bias divider.

The 16-pin VQFN repeats each output on the input side (FB+, FB–) so the feedback resistors sit right at the inputs, or a feedback capacitor can be added there for filters. Each internal trace adds about 3.3 Ω (3.0 Ω to 4.7 Ω at 25 °C) in series, which the TINA-TI model leaves out. On the 10-pin WQFN the outputs and inputs share one side, so the feedback resistors go hard against the package.

PD is a CMOS input with no pull-up and must be driven. It is referenced to VS–: above (VS–) + 1.15 V the amplifier runs, below (VS–) + 0.55 V it is off, so on a single supply it works from 1.8-V logic, and with a negative supply the off level must be below ground. Off, quiescent current is 1 µA typ, but the external resistors still pass the signal, so isolation is poor, and the input protection diodes can still conduct and draw supply current under large inputs. Turn-on takes about 700 ns and turn-off about 100 ns at 5 V.

VOCM sets the average of the two outputs. Left open it defaults close to midsupply for any supply split; driven, it is a high-impedance input (150 kΩ || 7 pF). An open pin is noisy: put a capacitor (0.1 µF) from it to ground. The common-mode loop stays linear with VOCM at least about 0.7 V above VS– and 1.3 V below VS+ over –40 °C to +125 °C (0.55 V and 1.2 V at 25 °C).

The inputs work down to the negative rail (0 V headroom, to (VS–) – 0.2 V typ at 25 °C) and need 1.3 V of headroom to VS+ over temperature. The outputs swing to within about 0.2 V of each rail for linear operation. Each output swings ±VOPP/4 around VOCM. With ac-coupled inputs the input pins sit at VOCM; with single-ended inputs they also move with the signal, by the output swing on the non-signal side divided back through RF and RG2.

RF = 1 kΩ is used for the characterization: it adds a 2-kΩ differential load across the outputs (667 Ω with a 1-kΩ load), keeps feedback power, 4kTRF noise and current-noise terms low, and keeps the pole from RF with the input capacitance manageable. Pick RF first, then RG for gain, then RT for a matched input. A differential source sees the sum of the two RG; a single-ended source sees more than RG because the input common mode follows the signal (1.33 kΩ with all resistors 1 kΩ). For best dc precision use 0.1% resistors.

With a dc-coupled source both inputs must be dc coupled to stay balanced; RG2 is usually grounded for a bipolar source or biased to the source's midpoint otherwise. VOCM drives a common-mode current back through RF and RG into the source, which the source must sink or supply, and which lifts the input pins above ground on a single supply. AC-coupled differential inputs need only blocking capacitors; an optional resistor across the inputs lowers the input impedance without changing gain.

Output offset collects VIO times the noise gain, IOS times RF, bias current times the RF mismatch (±2·T·RF), and any common-mode term (VOCM, source common mode, VOCM-path offset) converted to differential by unequal feedback ratios G1 and G2. With standard-value matched inputs the ratio mismatch, not resistor tolerance, often dominates; matching the networks on the two sides improves it. Drift is dominated by input offset voltage drift in the worked example (±3.82 µV/°C total).

A capacitive load straight on the outputs can make the loop unstable; put a series resistor RO in each output (the recommended-RO curves give values; higher gain needs less). Leave pads for RO even where 0 Ω works. The output stage's open-loop impedance turns inductive at high frequency, so feedback capacitors above about 100 pF can erode phase margin; 10 Ω to 15 Ω in series with the feedback capacitor reduces this. With only a feedback capacitor, noise gain falls to 1 V/V at high frequency; a capacitor across the inputs raises it again and restores margin, so leave a place for one in any filter.

Distortion comes mainly from the output stage's open-loop nonlinearity divided by loop gain. It rises with heavier loads (including the feedback resistors), larger swings and higher noise gain, and stays nearly constant as VOCM moves within range; clipping into either rail degrades it fast. Mismatched feedback ratios do not by themselves add distortion.

At low noise gain (attenuation, or large RF) phase margin drops; the 0.1-V/V design peaks about 5 dB from 32° of margin. Capacitors across RF plus one across the inputs shape the noise gain from NG1 up to NG2 above a chosen zero ZO, flattening the response at the cost of noise above ZO, which a following RC filter removes.

When the output reaches the rails and the input keeps rising, internal protection diodes (two in series each way) clamp the input pins to about 1.5 V differential; the input resistors limit the diode current. Recovery from 2X overdrive takes about 50 ns at 5 V.

Use a single 2.7-V to 5.4-V supply or split supplies totalling under 5.5 V. Put 0.1 µF at the supply pins of each part (one cap shared by the four VS+ pins on RGT) and a larger 2.2 µF further away, shareable among parts; on split supplies decouple both rails to ground. Ferrite beads between the large and local capacitors help with several channels. Keep supply edges slower than ±1 V/µs. The supply current has a PTAT bias, rising about 3.9 µA/°C at 5 V.
For linear swing to 0 V the negative rail can be taken slightly below ground, for example –230 mV from an LM7705 running from the same 3-V to 5-V supply.

Internal dissipation is the quiescent power plus the output stage power. Worked example: 5.4 V × 1.75 mA = 9.45 mW, plus (5.4 V – 2.7 V) × 1.35 mA = 3.65 mW into a 200-Ω differential load, 13.1 mW in all; at 163 °C/W in the WQFN this is a 2.1 °C rise, 127 °C at 125 °C ambient. Solder the RGT thermal pad to a power or ground plane.

Open the ground and power planes under and around the input and output pins, which are sensitive to capacitance. Keep each RG's pin-side end short into the summing junction; its far end can run longer. Place 0.1-µF decoupling at the power pins (X2Y capacitors resonate higher) and 2.2 µF further off. Route longer differential runs as matched-impedance microstrip. Use the RGT feedback pins to keep the feedback path short.
